ideas.title: Calina plans the story first: a spine and a 'because/but' link on every scene, checked in code
ideas.problem: CALINA_SYSTEM_V3 describes the 7 beats only in prose (agents.py ~l.634-642). The schema (EPISODE_SCHEMA_V3) has `storyline` as one free line and no per-scene logic. So the model can write fluent sentences that do not follow from each other, which is what the owner heard on ep 14 ('zero sense'). Israa's stranger test (quality.stranger_script) catches it only after a full script is written and costs a worker run; its rework asks Calina to try again with no structure to fix.
ideas.proposal:
1) In EPISODE_SCHEMA_V3 add required `spine` (object: once, every_day, one_day, because1, because2, finally, question_answered_in_scene) and in SCENE_SCHEMA add required `link` (enum: because|but|so|first|therefore) plus `step_claim` (one plain sentence: what the viewer now knows that they did not before). Scene 1's link is 'first'.
2) In the prompt, replace the line 'Follow this shape, in this order, and make each beat clear before the next:' with:
'Before writing any scene, write the `spine` and decide the ENDING first: the last scene must answer the hook question, and `question_answered_in_scene` names it. Then write each scene so it follows from the one before it with because, but, or so. If the only honest link between two scenes is "and then", the scene is a list item: cut it or merge it. At most two scenes in a Short may use link=first.'
3) Add to the batch validator (where episodes without sources are dropped, agents.py near calina_batch): reject/return-to-Calina any episode where the hook question's answer scene is not in the last 3 scenes, where more than 2 scenes have link 'first', or where any `step_claim` is empty. Pure Python, no extra LLM call.
4) Pass `spine` and the links to Israa's review task so her notes can name the exact broken link (quality.review_scripts).
ideas.gain: Moves 'does it make sense' from a late, paid check to a free structural check at write time. Measure: share of scripts that pass Israa's stranger test on round 1 (read from episodes.data.review.rounds); today's baseline from the episodes table, target at least 70% on round 1, and fewer reworks per batch.
ideas.test: 1) Normal: ask Calina for 2 scripts on a story with a clear cause chain (e.g. Eratosthenes); pass = every scene has a link, no 'and then' links, last 3 scenes answer the hook, stranger test true on all four keys. 2) Edge: a story where facts are a list (e.g. 'five odd Roman laws'); pass = Calina either finds a causal frame or says in `note` the topic does not fit a spine, instead of inventing links. 3) Failure: HQ_SIMULATE canned episode whose answer scene is scene 2 of 12; pass = validator rejects it with a message naming the rule, and the rewrite request quotes it.
ideas.confidence_why: Pixar rule 4/7 (B) and the but/therefore method (B) are practitioner craft, not experiments; the code-check part is certain to work. Weakest link: no measured retention gain.
ideas.risks: Schema fields add output tokens (about 10-15 words a scene). A model can fill `link` dishonestly, so the stranger test stays as the real judge. Changes the V3 schema: simulate.py's canned episodes and the seed eratosthenes.json need the new fields.

ideas.title: Show Calina 3 finished examples (and 2 bad ones), and add a free 'ear check' before Israa
ideas.problem: The V3 prompt has rules but zero worked examples, and Anthropic's guide calls examples 'one of the most reliable ways to steer output format, tone and structure' and recommends 3-5, diverse, in <example> tags. The only script file in the repo, animation/episodes/eratosthenes.json, is the old telegram style the prompt now forbids ('Noon. No shadow.'), so it must not be used as an example. Separately, 'full human sentences' is checked only by an LLM; fragments and equal-length sentences are easy to detect in code.
ideas.proposal:
1) Write 3 gold scripts (different eras and shapes, each 140-200 words, owner-approved by reading, not rendering) and 2 short bad-to-good rewrites using the owner's own ep 14 lines. Put them in a new file `calina_examples.md` shipped with main and inject into CALINA_SYSTEM_V3 inside <examples><example>...</example></examples>, placed ABOVE the instructions per the same guide ('longform data at the top'). Add: 'The examples show quality and shape. Never reuse their places, people or phrases.' The existing sameness check (idea 2026-10-04-1) guards against copying.
2) New function `ear_lint(scenes)` in quality.py, stdlib only, run before the Israa call: flag (a) three or more consecutive voice lines under 5 words (fragment chain), (b) lines with no verb-like word (simple check: no word from a short verb list or ending in -s/-ed/-ing is weak, so keep this rule to under-5-words only), (c) two or more consecutive sentences within 2 words of each other in length, (d) any sentence over 24 words, (e) digits in voice lines. Return a list that is passed to Calina's rewrite note. It never blocks by itself on (c); (a),(d),(e) send the script back once.
3) Show the lint result in the episode's review block.
ideas.gain: Fewer rounds with Israa (each round is a worker run) and the owner's 'toddler saying random words' problem is caught in milliseconds. Measure: count of lint flags per batch before/after, and owner rejections with the reason 'weak words'.
ideas.test: 1) Normal: a good gold script run through ear_lint returns an empty list. 2) Edge: a deliberate dramatic fragment run ('Noon. No shadow. Silence.') returns flag (a) but a single fragment between long sentences does not. 3) Failure: ep 14's text, if available from episodes.data, must produce at least 2 flags; if it produces none, the thresholds are wrong and must be fixed before shipping.
ideas.confidence_why: Anthropic's prompting guide on examples (A); fragment-chain and uniform-length heuristics came only from search snippets (C), so thresholds must be tuned on ep 14 and the approved episodes before trusting them.
ideas.risks: Calina may copy gold examples; mitigated by the sameness check and the 'never reuse' line. Examples add input tokens (about 700 words, roughly 1k tokens a batch), small next to the web searches. Lint thresholds can reject good dramatic writing; keep (c) advisory.
